source.title: Accurate, Large Minibatch SGD: Training ImageNet in 1 Hour
source.authors: Priya Goyal; Piotr Dollár; Ross B. Girshick; P. Noordhuis; L. Wesolowski; Aapo Kyrola; Andrew Tulloch; Yang-Qing Jia; Kaiming He

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly compares large- and small-minibatch SGD on ImageNet, measuring training and validation error under fixed 90-epoch schedules and testing warmup and learning-rate scaling choices.
record.gate_note: Rows cover ImageNet classification error under the reported batch-size and warmup conditions. COCO transfer and throughput results do not measure the in-distribution train–test gap named by the claim. Cited results from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V5 by comparing held-out ImageNet error across SGD batch sizes under the same 90-epoch budget, including learning-rate scaling and warmup conditions. It is an original source for V5, so no verdict labels are assigned.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that linear learning-rate scaling and gradual warmup allow ResNet-50 to match small-batch training and validation performance through batch 8192 within 90 epochs. They attribute failures mainly to optimization difficulties; errors increase beyond that range. ResNet-101 and ImageNet-5k show small residual penalties at 8k.
record.recipe_differences: Direct large-minibatch SGD comparison, but the study adapts learning rate linearly with batch size and adds gradual warmup; other hyperparameters and the 90-epoch schedule are held fixed.
record.method_sensitivity: ImageNet error depends on batch size and warmup: no or constant warmup harms the 8k result, gradual warmup brings it near baseline; errors rise at 16k and larger. The paper also reports a somewhat larger increase for ResNet-101 at 8k.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet pretraining with batches 256–8k yields nearly identical downstream COCO box and mask AP; pretraining at 16k lowers both.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-batch pretraining can preserve downstream transfer performance when source-task validation accuracy is preserved.

fits_no_version.finding: Mask R-CNN training with linearly scaled learning rates preserves box and mask AP across batch sizes 2–16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate scaling can preserve detection and segmentation performance across training batch sizes.

record.problems: The main batch-size comparisons are ImageNet classification experiments with one architecture family; the paper reports five trials for ResNet-50 error estimates but does not report uncertainty for the ResNet-101 comparison. The study does not test random labels or measure properties tracking the gap.
record.rows_left_out: COCO transfer AP, Mask R-CNN batch scaling, alternative learning-rate-only comparisons, training curves without separately stated numeric values, and throughput results were omitted because they do not directly measure the in-distribution classification train–test gap targeted by the versions. The ImageNet-5k results are retained as a dataset condition.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width scaling beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.

Language models; longer training as a remedy; other epoch budgets; normalization or regularization changes as independently tested remedies. The main successful recipe changes learning rate and warmup together.
Adding or removing dropout and its dependence on training-set size.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Batch-size comparison under standard BN initialization: batch 256 gives 23.84 ±0.18% error and batch 8k gives 24.11 ±0.07%, versus 23.60 ±0.12% and 23.74 ±0.09% with the modified initialization. This measures recipe dependence and is not declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: No labels are assigned because arXiv:1706.02677 is an original source for V5. Row states describe the presence of the large-batch penalty; its absence under an adapted recipe is explicitly accommodated by V5. Higher validation error here should not automatically be described as a larger train–test gap: training error also rises in unsuccessful large-batch conditions. The record's claim that ResNet-101 uncertainty is unreported is incorrect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width scaling beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language models; batches beyond those tested; alternative epoch budgets; whether some classifiers match small-batch accuracy under fixed epochs without adapting the recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other measured properties tracking the gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

relation.reason: Own experiments measure the large-batch penalty and its recovery with linear learning-rate scaling and gradual warmup.

tranche.reason: Original V5 source directly comparing ImageNet validation error across SGD minibatch sizes under a fixed 90-epoch budget.

source_check.notes: R4 and R10 duplicate the same result. Reported errors average five independent runs, each summarized by its median error over the final five epochs; uncertainty is between-run standard deviation. The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate.
